memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Heshbon was the city of Sihon king of the Amorites, who had fought against the former king of Moab and had taken from him all his land as far as the Arnon. That is why the poets say: "Come to Heshbon and let it be rebuilt; let Sihon's city be restored. Fire went out from Heshbon, a blaze from the city of Sihon. It consumed Ar of Moab, the citizens of Arnon's heights." - Num 21:26-28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
These verses record a piece of history through an old poem. Sihon had once conquered this land from Moab, and his city Heshbon had been celebrated as mighty and secure. The poem boasts of the fire that went out from Heshbon, consuming its enemies.

There is a sobering irony here. The very city that had triumphed over others now fell to Israel. The stronghold that once seemed unconquerable changed hands. Human power, however impressive, is never permanent. Kingdoms rise and fall, and today's conqueror can become tomorrow's conquered.

Scripture often pauses to show us the fragility of earthly might. It is a gentle warning against placing our confidence in things that cannot last. Cities crumble, empires fade, and the strong are humbled in time. Nothing built by human hands endures forever.

Where, then, should we build our hope? Not on any earthly power or possession, but on the kingdom that cannot be shaken. In Christ we belong to a kingdom that will never fall, ruled by a King whose throne is forever (Heb 12:28). Let your security rest there, in the One whose reign no army can overthrow.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where are you tempted to place your confidence in things that cannot last?
2. How does the fall of Heshbon remind you of the fragility of earthly power?
3. What does it mean for you to build your hope on Christ's unshakable kingdom?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep me from trusting in things that fade and fall. Anchor my hope in Your unshakable kingdom and in Christ my King, whose reign endures forever. Amen.
